# Command-line reference

This reference is generated from the same Clap definitions used by the `wavlab` executable.

## `wavlab`

```text
Inspect and process PCM WAV files

Usage: wavlab <COMMAND>

Commands:
  metadata              Load and display a WAV file's metadata
  normalize             Normalize the peak level to 0 dBFS
  normalize-db          Normalize the peak to a specified level in dBFS
  gain                  Multiply every sample by a linear gain factor
  gain-db               Apply an amplitude gain measured in decibels
  reverse               Reverse the audio while preserving the channel order in each frame
  flip-phase            Invert the polarity of every sample
  swap-channels         Swap the left and right channels of a stereo file
  split-stereo          Split a stereo WAV file into separate mono left and right files
  split-mid-side        Split a stereo WAV file into separate mono mid and side files
  split                 Split a WAV file at one or more millisecond positions
  left-right-to-stereo  Combine separate mono left and right WAV files into stereo
  mid-side-to-stereo    Decode separate mono mid and side WAV files into stereo
  mix                   Mix two or more WAV files starting at the first frame
  join                  Join two or more compatible WAV files end-to-end
  help                  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `wavlab metadata`

```text
Load and display a WAV file's metadata

Usage: wavlab metadata [OPTIONS] <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          WAV file to inspect

Options:
  -f, --full
          Load and scan samples to include peak and RMS levels

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab normalize`

```text
Normalize the peak level to 0 dBFS

Usage: wavlab normalize <INPUT> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab normalize-db`

```text
Normalize the peak to a specified level in dBFS

Usage: wavlab normalize-db <INPUT> <TARGET_DB> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <TARGET_DB>
          Target peak level in dBFS. Positive values may cause clipping

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab gain`

```text
Multiply every sample by a linear gain factor

Usage: wavlab gain <INPUT> <GAIN> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <GAIN>
          Linear gain factor. Magnitudes greater than 1 may cause clipping

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab gain-db`

```text
Apply an amplitude gain measured in decibels

Usage: wavlab gain-db <INPUT> <GAIN_DB> [OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to process

  <GAIN_DB>
          Gain in dB. Positive values may cause clipping

  [OUTPUT]
          Destination WAV file; defaults to overwriting the input file

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab split-stereo`

```text
Split a stereo WAV file into separate mono left and right files

Usage: wavlab split-stereo <INPUT> [LEFT_OUTPUT] [RIGHT_OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          Stereo WAV file to split

  [LEFT_OUTPUT]
          Destination for the left channel; omit both outputs to derive them

  [RIGHT_OUTPUT]
          Destination for the right channel; omit both outputs to derive them

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab split-mid-side`

```text
Split a stereo WAV file into separate mono mid and side files

Usage: wavlab split-mid-side <INPUT> [MID_OUTPUT] [SIDE_OUTPUT]

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          Stereo WAV file to split

  [MID_OUTPUT]
          Destination for the mid signal; omit both outputs to derive them

  [SIDE_OUTPUT]
          Destination for the side signal; omit both outputs to derive them

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab split`

```text
Split a WAV file at one or more millisecond positions

Usage: wavlab split <INPUT> <SPLIT_TIMES_MS>...

Arguments:
  <INPUT>
          WAV file to split

  <SPLIT_TIMES_MS>...
          Increasing split positions in milliseconds from the start

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab mix`

```text
Mix two or more WAV files starting at the first frame

Usage: wavlab mix <OUTPUT> <INPUTS> <INPUTS>...

Arguments:
  <OUTPUT>
          Destination mixed WAV file

  <INPUTS> <INPUTS>...
          Input WAV files to mix

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `wavlab join`

```text
Join two or more compatible WAV files end-to-end

Usage: wavlab join <OUTPUT> <INPUTS> <INPUTS>...

Arguments:
  <OUTPUT>
          Destination joined WAV file

  <INPUTS> <INPUTS>...
          Input WAV files to join in order

Options:
  -h, --help
          Print help
```
